Similar to the distortion pattern of the 39.6 m diameter tank floor [4], a long red region, indicating high distortion, forms and extends along the free space between the well-aligned short-edge welds parallel to the x-axis. 16 This report is available at no cost from the National Laboratory of the Rockies (NLR) at www.nlr.gov/publications. 2.3.2 Welding Model for the 32 m Diameter Tank Floor The 32 m diameter hot tank floor model is also formulated by the welding assembly of 347H stainless steel thin rectangular plates. Similar to the 24 m diameter tank floor model, the shell element model was built for half of the tank floor and implemented in Abaqus software. Figure 22 presents the layout of the 32 m diameter tank floor and the dimensions of the rectangular plates. Figure 22. Layout of the hot tank floor used in the 32 m diameter tank floor fabrication model. Based on the evaluation results presented in the previous report [4], the meshing strategy with minimum size of 8*20mm2 was adopted for the 32 m diameter tank floor model. Figure 23 presents the mesh model of the 32 m diameter tank floor. With this meshing strategy, the model includes 87,052 elements and 85,212 nodes. The element type setup is the same as the 24 m diameter model. A mixture of four- node linear quadrilateral and three-node linear triangular element types was used in the heat transfer (defined as DS4/DS3) and non-linear elastic-plastic calculations (S4R/S3R). Since the only difference between the 32 m and the 24 m diameter model is the dimension of the tank floor, all the model setups—including shell element properties, heat source parameters, simulation type, analysis steps, and the activation mode of long-edge elements—are the same as the 24 m diameter model. Therefore, the same welding simulation scheme and welding simulation steps presented in Figure 16 and Table 2 also apply to the 32 m diameter tank floor model. Figure 23 presents the temperature contours of the 32 m diameter tank floor at half of the welding time of the short-edge welding and the long-edge welding, respectively.
